summary.headline: Heatwaves have decreased by 16.7% in New Delhi, India since 2000.

key_findings.title: Decadal Frequency & Exposure Shift
key_findings.detail: Comparing the early period (2000–2009) to the most recent period (2011–2020), mean annual heatwave frequency shifted from 2.4 to 2.0 events/year (-16.7%), while annual heatwave days shifted from 14.3 to 11.4 days/year (-20.3%).

key_findings.title: Statistical Trend Verification (Mann-Kendall & OLS)
key_findings.detail: Linear regression indicates a rate of -0.39 events/decade (R² = 0.03, p = 0.423). The non-parametric Mann-Kendall test yields Z = -0.88 (τ = -0.14, p = 0.377): Downward Tendency (Not Statistically Significant).

key_findings.title: Duration & Persistence Dynamics
key_findings.detail: Average event duration went from 5.9 days (2000–2009) to 6.2 days (2011–2020). Peak seasonal clustering occurs during May, Jun, Apr, with 2010 recording the highest burden (35 heatwave days across 4 events).

key_findings.title: Background Climatological Shift
key_findings.detail: Across 2000–2020, regional mean daily maximum temperature changed at -0.40 °C/decade (p = 0.100). Even small shifts in the mean distribution tail disproportionately amplify 95th-percentile extremes.

critical_thinking_caveats: Sample Window Notice: The selected 21-year window (2000–2020) is shorter than the WMO 30-year standard reference period. Decadal climate modes (e.g., El Niño–Southern Oscillation) can influence short-period slopes.

Statistical Uncertainty: While the point estimate shows a -16.7% shift between the first and last 10-year windows, the Mann-Kendall test (p = 0.377) does not cross the strict α = 0.05 threshold due to high year-to-year variance. Interpret headline percentages alongside the confidence statistics.

summary.headline: Heavy rainfall events have increased by 61.1% in Mumbai, India since 1990.

key_findings.title: Decadal Frequency & Exposure Shift
key_findings.detail: Comparing the early period (1990–1999) to the most recent period (2015–2024), mean annual heavy rainfall frequency shifted from 3.6 to 5.8 events/year (+61.1%), while annual extreme rain days shifted from 5.5 to 9.0 days/year (+63.6%).

key_findings.title: Statistical Trend Verification (Mann-Kendall & OLS)
key_findings.detail: Linear regression indicates a rate of +0.86 events/decade (R² = 0.21, p = 0.005). The non-parametric Mann-Kendall test yields Z = +2.83 (τ = +0.33, p = 0.005): Significantly Increasing (p < 0.05).

key_findings.title: Duration & Persistence Dynamics
key_findings.detail: Average event duration went from 1.5 days (1990–1999) to 1.5 days (2015–2024). Peak seasonal clustering occurs during Jul, Jun, Aug, with 2022 recording the highest burden (14 extreme rain days across 6 events).

key_findings.title: Background Climatological Shift
key_findings.detail: Across 1990–2024, regional mean daily maximum temperature changed at +0.15 °C/decade (p = 0.010). Even small shifts in the mean distribution tail disproportionately amplify 95th-percentile extremes.

critical_thinking_caveats: High Statistical Confidence: Both parametric OLS regression and the non-parametric Mann-Kendall test confirm a statistically significant monotonic signal (p < 0.05), indicating that the observed change is unlikely to be random inter-annual noise.

summary.headline: Drought / dry-spell events have decreased by 6.3% in Rajasthan (State), India since 1990.

key_findings.title: Decadal Frequency & Exposure Shift
key_findings.detail: Comparing the early period (1990–1999) to the most recent period (2015–2024), mean annual drought frequency shifted from 6.4 to 6.0 events/year (-6.3%), while annual dry-spell days shifted from 265.6 to 258.5 days/year (-2.7%).

key_findings.title: Statistical Trend Verification (Mann-Kendall & OLS)
key_findings.detail: Linear regression indicates a rate of -0.09 events/decade (R² = 0.00, p = 0.736). The non-parametric Mann-Kendall test yields Z = -0.39 (τ = -0.05, p = 0.695): No Statistically Significant Monotonic Trend.

key_findings.title: Duration & Persistence Dynamics
key_findings.detail: Average event duration went from 43.0 days (1990–1999) to 44.8 days (2015–2024). Peak seasonal clustering occurs during Sep, Oct, Feb, with 1999 recording the highest burden (356 dry-spell days across 6 events).

key_findings.title: Background Climatological Shift
key_findings.detail: Across 1990–2024, regional mean daily maximum temperature changed at +0.16 °C/decade (p = 0.136). Even small shifts in the mean distribution tail disproportionately amplify 90th-percentile extremes.

critical_thinking_caveats: Statistical Uncertainty: While the point estimate shows a -6.3% shift between the first and last 10-year windows, the Mann-Kendall test (p = 0.695) does not cross the strict α = 0.05 threshold due to high year-to-year variance.
